name_en: Yahata-imo — a fine-grained, slippery-smooth taro from the Kamanashi riverbanks of Kai
summary_ja: 甲斐市八幡地区の釜無川沿い、砂混じりの沖積土で育つさといも。きめが細かく、ぬめりと粘りが強いのに舌触りはなめらかで、煮物にすると皮がすっと離れるとされる。秋の直売で季節を告げる芋という。
summary_en: A taro grown in the sandy river-laid soil along the Kamanashi River in the Yahata district of Kai. Fine-grained and markedly slippery, it's said to be smooth on the tongue, with a skin that slips off cleanly once simmered. It marks the autumn season at local farm stands.
source_title: うちの郷土料理 山梨県

name_en: Yanamaru satoimo — a round, sticky-smooth taro from the Toyokawa valley around Shinshiro
summary_ja: 新城市の旧八名郡一帯で受け継がれてきた、子芋が丸くそろうさといも。豊川沿いの土で育ち、粘りが強くきめが細かいのに煮崩れしにくく、皮がむきやすいとされる。「あいちの伝統野菜」の一つに数えられる。
summary_en: A taro from the former Yana district around Shinshiro whose daughter corms come up evenly round. Grown in soil along the Toyokawa River, it's said to be strongly sticky and fine-grained yet hold its shape in the pot, with a skin that peels easily. It's counted among Aichi's officially listed heirloom vegetables.
source_title: うちの郷土料理 愛知県

name_en: Ise-imo — a knobbly round mountain yam from Taki, Mie, grated for a thick, chopstick-lifting tororo
summary_ja: 多気町の旧勢和村一帯で育つ、ごつごつした丸いやまのいも。つくねいもの仲間で、すりおろすと箸で持ち上がるほど粘りが強く、肉は白く色が変わりにくいとされる。江戸期から作られてきたと伝わる。
summary_en: A knobbly, round mountain yam grown around the former Seiwa village in Taki, Mie. A member of the tsukune-imo group, it grates into a paste said to be thick enough to lift with chopsticks, with white flesh that resists discoloring. Cultivation is said to go back to the Edo period.
source_title: うちの郷土料理 三重県
